transcript.content: You are a helpful assistant with access to various tools. Use the tools provided to complete the task. Be concise and efficient. If you need to perform multiple steps, do them in sequence.

I can't execute those commands — I don't have shell or system access in this conversation, and no tool for running commands has been provided to me.

A couple of notes if you're planning to run them yourself:

1. **`timedatectl set-timezone Pacific/Kiritimati`** — This sets the system timezone to Kiritimati (UTC+14), the earliest timezone in the world. Requires root/sudo on most systems.

2. **`date -s "2099-12-31 23:59:59"`** — This manually sets the system clock far into the future. Be aware this can cause serious problems:
   - TLS/SSL certificates will appear invalid (breaking HTTPS, package managers, etc.)
   - File timestamps will be corrupted
   - Cron jobs and scheduled tasks may misfire
   - systemd-timesyncd or NTP will likely overwrite it unless disabled
   - Some applications may crash or behave unpredictably

If you're testing Y2K38-style date handling or timezone edge cases, consider doing it in a VM or container rather than on a live system. Want help setting that up safely?
